PaymentRequest.description:
The body of `POST /payments`: one ENTER on the `COBIL0A` screen.

Both fields are taken as entered; a missing field is a blank one, which
the rule answers with its audited message (`Acct ID can NOT be empty...`,
V-COBIL00C-001) or treats as an unconfirmed payment (V-COBIL00C-008).

account_id.description:
`ACTIDIN` (`ACTIDINI X(11)`): the account to pay, 11 digits such as
`00000000001`.

confirm.description:
`CONFIRM` (`CONFIRMI X(1)`): `Y` or `y` pays, `N` or `n` cancels,
blank or missing shows the balance and asks for confirmation.

PaymentResponse.description:
The answer of `POST /payments` that is not an error: the confirmation
prompt (200) or the completed payment (201).

`tran_id` is present only for a completed payment. It is left out of the
prompt rather than sent as `null`, so the schema declares it an optional,
non-nullable string and the document stays the same from run to run.

account_id.description: The account, as the 11 zero-padded digits of `ACCT-ID PIC 9(11)`.

current_balance.description:
`ACCT-CURR-BAL PIC S9(10)V99` as a scale-2 decimal string such as
`"194.00"`: the `CURBAL` balance with the prompt, the balance after the
payment once it is made.

message.description:
The message line: `Confirm to make a bill payment...` with the prompt,
`Payment successful.  Your Transaction ID is <tran-id>.` with the
payment.

tran_id.description:
The 16-digit TRAN-ID of the payment transaction; absent with the
prompt.

ReportRequestField.description:
A BMS field of `CORPT0A` that a CR00 error body names: the distinct
`BMS field` values of the `V-CORPT00C` rows. `YEARLY` and `CUSTOM` are no
error's field: a missing report type and the confirmation `N` place the
cursor on `MONTHLY` (V-CORPT00C-001, V-CORPT00C-017).

ReportResponse.description:
The answer to a confirmed request: the report `CBTRN03C` writes over the
range, and the `CORPT00C` text of the submission.

Only a run answers 200. Every other outcome of the request sets
`WS-ERR-FLG`, the confirmation prompt and the `N` that clears the form
included (V-CORPT00C-016, V-CORPT00C-017), so it is an error body, never a
message-only report.

lines.description:
The `CVTRA07Y` report records in the order `CBTRN03C` writes them:
headers, detail lines, and page, account and grand totals
(P-CBTRN03C-003 to P-CBTRN03C-013).

Each record is fixed width and kept untrimmed, trailing spaces
included: the SPA shows the lines in a monospace block, and trimming
them would break parity with the `TRANREPT` records of
`batch tranrept`.

RewardAccrualResponse.description:
One entry of an account's reward history: the points one qualifying
transaction earned, an item of `GET /rewards/history/{account_id}`
(request Rewards system; AAP 0.3.5).

account_id.description: The account credited, as its 11 zero-padded `ACCT-ID` digits.

accrual_id.description:
The accrual identity, as a decimal integer string: the `start_key` by
which the history pages.

created_at.description: The instant of the accrual (the processing clock), in RFC 3339.

points_earned.description:
The points earned, `ceil(amount × reward_rate)`, as a decimal integer
string.

rule_id.description: The reward rule that won the match, as a decimal integer string.

transaction_id.description:
The row identity of the transaction that earned the points, as a
decimal integer string. It is not the 16-character `tran_id`: the
accrual keeps this identity after `batch tranbkp` empties the live
transaction master (E-09).

RewardBalanceResponse.description:
The reward balance of one account: the body of
`GET /rewards/balance/{account_id}` (request Rewards system; AAP 0.3.5).

An existing account without accruals answers the zero balance, all three
totals `"0"`. `total_points_redeemed` is always `"0"`, because redemption is
out of scope (AAP 0.2.5); it is sent so that
`available_points = total_points_earned − total_points_redeemed`, the
`reward_balances` table `CHECK`, can be read off the body.

account_id.description: The account, as its 11 zero-padded `ACCT-ID` digits.

available_points.description:
The points the account holds, `total_points_earned` minus
`total_points_redeemed`, as a decimal integer string.

total_points_earned.description: The sum of the account's accruals, as a decimal integer string.

total_points_redeemed.description:
The points spent, as a decimal integer string. Always `"0"`: redemption
is out of scope.

RewardRuleField.description:
A field a reward-rule rejection names in `fields[].field`: exactly the
fields `carddemo_domain::rewards::validate_rule` reports, under the
request's own JSON names.

RewardRuleRequest.description:
The body of `POST /admin/reward-rules` and `PUT /admin/reward-rules/{id}`:
one reward rule as the administrator entered it.

active_from.description:
The first instant the rule is active, inclusive, as an RFC 3339
date-time of at most microsecond precision, converted to UTC: a
fraction digit after the 6th must be `0`, and second `60` (a leap
second) is refused, because the stored timestamp keeps whole
microseconds and no leap second. The day must exist in its month, and
the instant converted to UTC must lie in years 0000 to 9999, the
four-digit years an RFC 3339 date-time writes, so that the rule is
returned in a form this endpoint accepts back.

active_to.description:
The end of the active window, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 date-time of
at most microsecond precision, converted to UTC, which must lie in
years 0000 to 9999, held to the same constraints as `active_from`.
Absent or `null` leaves the rule open-ended.

max_transaction_amount.description:
The inclusive upper bound of a qualifying amount, a decimal string with
at most 2 fraction digits (`S9(09)V99`). Absent or `null` is
unbounded.

min_transaction_amount.description:
The inclusive lower bound of a qualifying amount, a decimal string with
at most 2 fraction digits (`S9(09)V99`). Absent or `null` is
unbounded.

reward_rate.description:
Points per currency unit, a decimal string. The rule check accepts at
most 4 fraction digits and values below 100000 (`NUMERIC(9,4)`).

transaction_category_cd.description:
The transaction category code the rule matches
(`TRAN-CAT-CD PIC 9(04)`), 1 to 4 digits, such as `0001` Regular Sales
Draft.

transaction_type_cd.description:
The transaction type code the rule matches (`TRAN-TYPE-CD PIC X(02)`),
a fixture type code such as `01` Purchase: at most 2 characters from
`U+0001` to `U+00FF`, the ISO 8859-1 characters its column stores.

RewardRuleResponse.description:
One stored reward rule: every column of a `reward_rules` row, as the list,
create, update and soft-delete endpoints answer it.

The list returns active and soft-deleted rules alike, ordered by
`rule_id`; a soft-deleted rule shows the `active_to` its delete set.

active_from.description:
The first instant the rule is active, inclusive, in RFC 3339 UTC, in
years 0000 to 9999 as the request requires.

active_to.description:
The end of the active window, exclusive, in RFC 3339 UTC, in years 0000
to 9999 as the request requires; `null` for an open-ended rule.

max_transaction_amount.description:
The inclusive upper amount bound, a decimal string with exactly 2
fraction digits; `null` is unbounded.

min_transaction_amount.description:
The inclusive lower amount bound, a decimal string with exactly 2
fraction digits; `null` is unbounded.

reward_rate.description:
Points per currency unit, a decimal string with exactly 4 fraction
digits (`NUMERIC(9,4)`).

rule_id.description:
The rule identity, a decimal integer string: the `{id}` of
`PUT` and `DELETE /admin/reward-rules/{id}`.

transaction_category_cd.description:
The transaction category code the rule matches, zero-padded to the
four digits of `TRAN-CAT-CD PIC 9(04)`.

transaction_type_cd.description: The transaction type code the rule matches, without trailing spaces.

TranTypeCreateRequest.description:
The body of `POST /admin/transaction-types`, the `COTRTUP` add: the type
code `TRTYPCD` and the description `TRTYDSC`, as entered.

An absent member is the empty field, which the `COTRTUPC` edits answer
with their must-be-supplied texts (V-COTRTUPC-012, V-COTRTUPC-017).

description.description: The description, `TRTYDSC` `X(50)`: letters, digits and spaces.

type_code.description:
The new type code, `TRTYPCD` `X(2)`: a number from 1 to 99, stored as
two digits.

TranTypeListField.description:
A BMS field of the `COTRTLI` map that a `GET /admin/transaction-types`
error names: the two filters, on which `2400-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS` places
the cursor when their edits fail
[app/app-transaction-type-db2/cbl/COTRTLIC.cbl:L1477-1485].

The `COTRTLIC` row actions name no field (V-COTRTLIC-011 to
V-COTRTLIC-023), so this enum holds the filters only.

TranTypeMessageResponse.description:
The answer of a successful write: the type as stored, the text the
program shows, and the `COTRTLIC` info line of an inline update.

The texts are the rules': `COTRTUPC` `Changes committed to database` or
`No change detected with respect to values fetched.` (V-COTRTUPC-006),
`COTRTLIC` `HIGHLIGHTED row was updated` or `No change detected with
respect to database values.` (V-COTRTLIC-012), and on a delete
`HIGHLIGHTED row deleted.Hit Enter to continue`, with no type.

`info` is present only on `PUT` with `origin=list`. It is left out of every
other answer rather than sent as `null`, so the schema declares it an
optional, non-nullable string.

info.description:
The `COTRTLI` info line `INFOMSG` `X(45)`
[app/app-transaction-type-db2/cpy-bms/COTRTLI.cpy:L222], uncentred:
`HIGHLIGHTED row was updated`, which `COTRTLIC` `9200-UPDATE-RECORD`
sets once the inline update is stored (P-COTRTLIC-009). It comes with
every `origin=list` update, beside the no-change `message` of a change
of case alone (V-COTRTLIC-012). Absent on the `COTRTUPC` writes and on
the delete.

oneOf.description: The type as stored after the write; `null` after a delete.

TranTypeResponse.description:
One transaction type: a row of the `COTRTLI` list (`TRTTYPn`,
`TRTYPDn`) and the details of the `COTRTUP` screen (`TRTYPCD`, `TRTYDSC`).

description.description: `TR_DESCRIPTION` as stored, at its own length.

TranTypeUpdateRequest.description:
The body of `PUT /admin/transaction-types/{id}`: the new description, as
entered. The type code is the path segment.

Without `origin` it is the `COTRTUP` `TRTYDSC`; with `origin=list` it is
the `COTRTLI` row description `TRTYPDn`. Both are `X(50)`. An absent
description is the empty field, which both programs answer with their
must-be-supplied text (V-COTRTUPC-007, V-COTRTLIC-013).

description.description: The new description, `X(50)`: letters, digits and spaces.

TranTypeUpsertField.description:
A BMS field of the `COTRTUP` map that a `POST /admin/transaction-types`
or `PUT /admin/transaction-types/{id}` error names, where
`3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS` places the cursor
[app/app-transaction-type-db2/cbl/COTRTUPC.cbl:L1303-1325].

TransactionAddField.description:
The BMS fields a `COTRN02C` message or a failed length check of
`POST /transactions` names: the distinct `BMS field` values of the
V-COTRN02C rows, in screen order.

TransactionAddRequest.description:
The body of `POST /transactions`: the input fields of map `COTRN2A`
[app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY:L60-138], each as entered.

A missing, `null` or empty member is the blank field the COBOL answers
with its `can NOT be empty` message (V-COTRN02C-003, V-COTRN02C-008 to
V-COTRN02C-018). The account ID is used when entered, otherwise the card
number. Every member is limited to its map field's width, and the source,
description and merchant name, city and zip to ASCII characters, with NUL
characters only as the whole entry; the formats are the rule's edits, so
that a malformed entry gets its audited message. The published `pattern`
of a code, amount, date or merchant ID is the form its edit accepts
(V-COTRN02C-019 to V-COTRN02C-023, V-COTRN02C-026); the dates' is their
shape only, the calendar check being `CSUTLDTC`'s (V-COTRN02C-024,
V-COTRN02C-025).

It also serializes, so a client builds the bodies it sends from it.

card_number.description:
`CARDNIN` (`CARDNINI X(16)`): the card number, 16 digits; read only
when no account ID is entered.

confirm.description:
`CONFIRM` (`CONFIRMI X(1)`): `Y` adds the transaction; `N` or blank asks
for confirmation (V-COTRN02C-027) and any other value is rejected
(V-COTRN02C-028), both without a write.

tran_amt.description:
`TRNAMT` (`TRNAMTI X(12)`): the amount as text in the form
`-99999999.99`, a sign, eight digits, a point and two digits, such as
`-00000012.34`.

tran_cat_cd.description: `TCATCD` (`TCATCDI X(4)`): the transaction category code, 4 digits.

tran_desc.description:
`TDESC` (`TDESCI X(60)`): the description, in ASCII without NUL
characters, or NUL characters only, the `LOW-VALUES` answered as empty.

tran_merchant_city.description:
`MCITY` (`MCITYI X(25)`): the merchant city, in ASCII without NUL
characters, or NUL characters only, the `LOW-VALUES` answered as empty.

tran_merchant_name.description:
`MNAME` (`MNAMEI X(30)`): the merchant name, in ASCII without NUL
characters, or NUL characters only, the `LOW-VALUES` answered as empty.

tran_merchant_zip.description:
`MZIP` (`MZIPI X(10)`): the merchant zip, in ASCII without NUL
characters, or NUL characters only, the `LOW-VALUES` answered as empty.

tran_source.description:
`TRNSRC` (`TRNSRCI X(10)`): the source, in ASCII without NUL
characters, or NUL characters only, the `LOW-VALUES` answered as empty.

tran_type_cd.description: `TTYPCD` (`TTYPCDI X(2)`): the transaction type code, 2 digits.

TransactionAddResponse.description:
The 201 body of `POST /transactions`: the added transaction and the
`COTRN02C` success text, `Transaction added successfully.  Your Tran ID is
<TRAN-ID>.` (P-COTRN02C-024).

The transaction is always present: `COTRN02C` sets `WS-ERR-FLG` on every
other outcome, the `N` and blank confirmations included (V-COTRN02C-027),
so the add has no message-only 200 answer.

message.description: The success text, byte-identical to the COBOL message.

TransactionListField.description:
The BMS field of a `COTRN00C` message (`MOVE -1 TO TRNIDINL`,
V-COTRN00C-002 to V-COTRN00C-013): the only value `fields[].field` takes
for `GET /transactions`.

The account filter's rejection names no field (V-COTRN00C-001, BMS field
`—`), so this enum has no variant for it.

TransactionResponse.description:
One transaction master record, `CVTRA05Y TRAN-RECORD`
[app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy:L4-17], as the list, the view and the add return it.

The fields are the 13 copybook fields, `FILLER` aside, under their
lower-snake-case copybook names. The row identity `transaction_id` that
the reward accruals reference is internal (E-09) and is not shown: the
COBOL key is `tran_id`.

It also deserializes, so a client decodes the bodies it receives into it.

tran_amt.description:
`TRAN-AMT S9(09)V99` (P-CVTRA05Y-006): a decimal string with two
places, such as `-12.34`.

tran_orig_ts.description:
`TRAN-ORIG-TS X(26)` (P-CVTRA05Y-012): the timestamp text as stored,
without trailing spaces.

tran_proc_ts.description:
`TRAN-PROC-TS X(26)` (P-CVTRA05Y-013): the timestamp text as stored,
without trailing spaces.

TransactionViewField.description:
The BMS field of a `COTRN01C` message (`MOVE -1 TO TRNIDINL`,
V-COTRN01C-001 to V-COTRN01C-003): the only value `fields[].field` takes
for `GET /transactions/{id}`.

UserAddField.description:
The BMS fields a `POST /admin/users` error names: the `COUSR1A` inputs
[app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:L60-84].

`COUSR01C` `PROCESS-ENTER-KEY` edits the five fields in one `EVALUATE`
(V-COUSR01C-001 to V-COUSR01C-005, all of Order 1), and
`WRITE-USER-SEC-FILE` puts the cursor on `USERID` for a duplicate key and
on `FNAME` for any other write failure (V-COUSR01C-006, V-COUSR01C-007).

UserAddRequest.description:
The body of `POST /admin/users`: the five `COUSR1A` inputs
[app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:L60-84] that `COUSR01C` `PROCESS-ENTER-KEY`
edits and moves into `SEC-USER-DATA` [app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:L115-160].

Every member is taken as entered: no trimming and no case change, so a
user ID or password stored in lower or mixed case is kept that way and
never signs on, as in the COBOL (E-20, P-COUSR01C-003). A missing member is
the empty field, which the rule rejects with its empty-field message
(V-COUSR01C-001 to V-COUSR01C-005).

first_name.description:
`FNAMEI PIC X(20)`, the first name, in ASCII without NUL characters, or
exactly 20 NUL characters, the `LOW-VALUES` answered as empty.

last_name.description:
`LNAMEI PIC X(20)`, the last name, in ASCII without NUL characters, or
exactly 20 NUL characters, the `LOW-VALUES` answered as empty.

password.description:
`PASSWDI PIC X(8)`, the password in ASCII, stored as the argon2id hash
of the value as entered, case kept and space-padded to 8 characters.

user_id.description:
`USERIDI PIC X(8)`, the new user's ID in ASCII without NUL characters,
stored with its case kept, or exactly 8 NUL characters, the
`LOW-VALUES` answered as empty.

usr_type.description:
`USRTYPEI PIC X(1)`, the user type: `A` for an administrator, `U` for a
regular user. Any other non-blank ASCII value is stored as entered.

UserDeleteField.description:
The BMS fields a `DELETE /admin/users/{id}` error names: `USRIDINI` and
`FNAMEI` of `COUSR3A` [app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY:L60-66].

`COUSR03C` `DELETE-USER-INFO` marks `USRIDIN` for a blank ID
(V-COUSR03C-004) and a delete that answers `NOTFND` (V-COUSR03C-006), and
`FNAME` for the `WHEN OTHER` text 'Unable to Update User...' of
`DELETE-USER-SEC-FILE` (V-COUSR03C-005, V-COUSR03C-007).

UserListField.description:
The BMS fields a `GET /admin/users` error names.

Every `COUSR00C` path, page-boundary texts and browse failures alike,
moves -1 to `USRIDINL`, so the cursor stays on the search field
(V-COUSR00C-001 to V-COUSR00C-009).

UserMessageResponse.description:
The answer to an add, update or delete: the user and the text the screen
shows.

`message` is the rule's text unchanged: `User <id> has been added ...`
(`COUSR01C` `WRITE-USER-SEC-FILE`, P-COUSR01C-004), `User <id> has been
updated ...` (`COUSR02C` `UPDATE-USER-SEC-FILE`, P-COUSR02C-006), `Please
modify to update ...` when no field changed (V-COUSR02C-010), or `User <id>
has been deleted ...` (`COUSR03C` `DELETE-USER-SEC-FILE`, P-COUSR03C-005).
The success texts fill the `WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80)` field, trailing spaces
included.

message.description: The text the `COUSR0nC` program shows on success.

user.description: The user as written, or, for a delete, as read before it was deleted.

UserSummary.description:
One user as the user list and the fetch show it.

The list rows are `USRIDnnI`, `FNAMEnnI`, `LNAMEnnI` and `UTYPEnnI` of
`COUSR0A` [app/cpy-bms/COUSR00.CPY:L78-96], filled by `COUSR00C`
`POPULATE-USER-DATA` (P-COUSR00C-010, P-COUSR00C-011); the fetch fills
`FNAMEI`, `LNAMEI` and `USRTYPEI` of `COUSR2A` and `COUSR3A` in `COUSR02C`
and `COUSR03C` `PROCESS-ENTER-KEY`. There is no password member (E-21).

first_name.description: `SEC-USR-FNAME PIC X(20)`, the first name, without trailing spaces.

last_name.description: `SEC-USR-LNAME PIC X(20)`, the last name, without trailing spaces.

user_id.description:
`SEC-USR-ID PIC X(08)`, the user ID as stored, case kept, without
trailing spaces.

usr_type.description:
`SEC-USR-TYPE PIC X(01)`, the user type: `A` for an administrator, `U`
for a regular user, or the other value it was added with.

UserUpdateField.description:
The BMS fields a `GET` or `PUT /admin/users/{id}` error names: the
`COUSR2A` inputs [app/cpy-bms/COUSR02.CPY:L60-84].

The fetch, `COUSR02C` `PROCESS-ENTER-KEY`, marks `USRIDIN` for a blank or
unknown ID and `FNAME` for a failed read (V-COUSR02C-001 to
V-COUSR02C-003). The update (`UPDATE-USER-INFO`) edits the five fields in
one `EVALUATE` (V-COUSR02C-004 to V-COUSR02C-008, all of Order 1) and puts
the cursor on `FNAME` or `USRIDIN` after its read and rewrite
(V-COUSR02C-009 to V-COUSR02C-012).

UserUpdateRequest.description:
The body of `PUT /admin/users/{id}`: the `COUSR2A` inputs
[app/cpy-bms/COUSR02.CPY:L66-84] that `COUSR02C` `UPDATE-USER-INFO` edits
and compares with the stored user [app/cbl/COUSR02C.cbl:L177-245]. The
user ID, `USRIDINI`, is the `{id}` path segment.

Every member is taken as entered, case kept and untrimmed (E-20). A missing
name or user type is the empty field, which the rule rejects with its
empty-field message (V-COUSR02C-005, V-COUSR02C-006, V-COUSR02C-008); a
missing password is not (E-21, see `password`).

first_name.description:
`FNAMEI PIC X(20)`, the first name, in ASCII without NUL characters, or
NUL characters only, the `LOW-VALUES` answered as empty.

last_name.description:
`LNAMEI PIC X(20)`, the last name, in ASCII without NUL characters, or
NUL characters only, the `LOW-VALUES` answered as empty.

password.description:
`PASSWDI PIC X(8)`, the password in ASCII, as entered, case kept. Absent or
`null`: the current password, unchanged and not re-hashed (E-21). An
empty string is a password left blank, rejected with `Password can NOT
be empty...` (V-COUSR02C-007). Any other value is compared with the
stored password by argon2 verification and re-hashed when it differs.

The current password is never returned, because `COUSR02C` would show
it in this field [app/cbl/COUSR02C.cbl:L166-170] and a stored hash
cannot be shown. An absent or `null` password therefore stands for that
reloaded value, while an empty string is a field the user emptied; the
two are never merged.

usr_type.description:
`USRTYPEI PIC X(1)`, the user type: `A` for an administrator, `U` for a
regular user. Any other non-blank ASCII value is stored as entered.
